title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Small Amount Credit Contract and Consumer Lease Reforms) Bill 2018 [No. 2]
short_title: National Consumer Credit Protection Amendment (Small Amount Credit Contract and Consumer Lease Reforms) Bill 2018 [No. 2]

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would implement recommendations from a 2016 review of small amount credit contract laws.
It would cap total payments under consumer leases, require equal repayments for small loans, ban door-to-door selling of leases at homes, and introduce anti-avoidance rules.
The bill also allows regulations to set a protected earnings amount for consumers of small loans and leases, preventing contracts that require too much of a person's income.
changes: Imposes a cap on total payments under consumer leases, which currently have no such cap.
Requires small amount credit contracts to have equal repayments and equal payment intervals.
Removes the ability for lenders to charge monthly fees on the remaining loan term when a consumer repays early.
Prevents lessors and credit assistance providers from selling leases door-to-door at homes.
Introduces broad anti-avoidance protections to stop providers from getting around the Credit Act and Code.
Strengthens penalties to encourage compliance by lenders and lessors.
summary.affected: Vulnerable Australians who use small amount credit contracts or consumer leases, as well as lenders and lessors in those industries.
